static_traits.name: Xia Jie
static_traits.family_status: Mother is a cancer survivor, rest not mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends, but avoids some socializing due to negative beliefs about appearance; finding it hard to discuss such insecurity with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological issues in the past; never received psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, organized thinking, able to self-reflect with high cooperativeness; positive attitude, moderate emotional expression

basic_info.main_problem: I believe no one wants to date me because I think I am ugly, even though I have not actively sought a partner. This thought pains me and affects my self-esteem.
basic_info.core_demands: Seeking counseling because negative beliefs about appearance and attractiveness are affecting overall well-being and social life; hoping to learn to more effectively identify and restructure these thoughts, using more realistic alternative perspectives, boosting confidence and self-esteem.
growth_experiences: About six months ago noticed decreased interest from potential dating prospects, gradually forming the belief that 'because I do not look good, no one wants to date me'; this belief intensified over time, affecting social life and self-esteem.
Past dating rejections were attributed to 'appearance issues', and negative beliefs and emotions are repeatedly reactivated when similar scenarios trigger them afterwards.

core_beliefs: I am not worthy of being loved
I am destined to be rejected

special_situations.event: When talking with someone of interest at a friend's party, the other person seemed not very interested
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the other person does not immediately show interest, it means my appearance is the problem
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Retreating on the spot, reducing proactive conversation and follow-up attempts, to avoid being rejected again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As expected, I am ugly; no one would want to date me

special_situations.event: Seeing happy couples on the street
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others can all find partners but I cannot, it means I am not worthy of being loved
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-denial after comparing with others, further avoiding social situations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot compare with others; I am destined to be wanted by no one

special_situations.event: Receiving any form of rejection or cold response
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If rejected, it proves my appearance has a fatal flaw, and it will always be so in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding potential dating opportunities and social contact to reduce the risk of being rejected
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: In the future I will only keep being rejected

special_situations.event: In the past six months, perceived that potential dating partners' interest in her has decreased
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If attention drops, it means I am increasingly without charm
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Labeling oneself 'ugly/unwanted' and trying to suppress negative thoughts with positive self-talk, but with poor results
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Everything is getting worse; I am increasingly unattractive

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be accepted and for intimacy
defense_goal: Reducing the pain of being rejected by keeping distance and avoiding
Explanations attributing things to appearance maintaining a sense of control

object_relations.object_representation: Critical others/potential partners who easily reject people

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about dating situations of being treated coldly or rejected
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to believe others hold negative evaluations of one's appearance (equating others' thoughts with negation of oneself)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Low, self-belittling tone, repeatedly emphasizing appearance as the main cause, slighting other possibilities; drawing conclusions in affirmative sentences, reducing pauses and exploration.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When needing to interpret 'why attention dropped/rejections increased'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Reducing complex interpersonal interactions to the single cause of 'not good-looking'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using seemingly rational causal chains to stress that looks determine everything, tone certain, avoiding discussion of other evidence or uncertainty.

manifestations: Directly equating being rejected with appearance, worrying no one will want an intimate relationship with oneself
Avoiding socializing, reducing contact with potential partners
outcomes: Social withdrawal and increased sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Automatically assuming others negate oneself because of appearance when narrating social situations
Directly interpreting the other's disinterest as negation of one's own worth

positive_force: Positive attitude, willing to seek help and learn alternative perspectives
Can propose other possible explanations in discussion, with some cognitive flexibility
Has better self-efficacy in non-intimate relationship areas; has transferable confidence resources
Has a few reliable friends who can provide some support
Has self-regulation and self-care habits such as reading and walking
negative_force: Highly dependent on external validation about appearance and acceptance
Frequent cognitive distortions like catastrophizing, mind reading and predicting the future
Social avoidance behaviors maintaining and worsening negative beliefs
Self-labeling ('ugly/wanted by no one') damaging self-esteem
Overgeneralizing past rejection experiences into stable self-attributes

antecedent: Thinking about one's appearance and how attractive one is
target_behavior.core_reason: Viewing appearance as the main cause of being rejected, generalizing past rejection experiences, forming strong worry about being rejected again and shame
target_behavior.function: Escaping possible negative evaluation and the pain of being rejected
target_behavior.consequence: Fewer dating and social opportunities, reinforcing the belief that 'no one wants to date me', further damaged self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Negative automatic thoughts and self-labeling (e.g. 'I am ugly, no one would want to date me')
antecedent: Unsuccessful social interactions or the other person seeming uninterested
Recalling past experiences of being rejected
Noticing a potential date's interest declining
target_behavior.core_reason: High dependence on external validation and mind-reading tendencies lead them to simplify complex interactions into the conclusion that appearance determines everything
target_behavior.function: Providing a 'controllable interpretation' for rejection, briefly easing uncertainty and anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, worsened hopelessness, and further triggering avoidant behavior
